(a) In General.—If the amount appropriated to carry out the essential air service program under subchapter II of chapter 417 of title 49, United States Code, equals or exceeds $110,000,000 for fiscal year 2007 or 2008, then the Secretary of Commerce shall make $15,000,000 available, from the Digital Television Transition and Public Safety Fund established by section 309(j)(8)(E) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j)(8)(E)), to the Secretary of Transportation for use in carrying out the essential air service program for that fiscal year. 
    (b) Application With Other Funds.—Amounts made available under subsection (a) for any fiscal year shall be in addition to any amounts—
        (1) appropriated for that fiscal year; or 
        (2) derived from fees collected pursuant to section 45301(a)(1) of title 49, United States Code, that are made available for obligation and expenditure to carry out the essential air service program for that fiscal year.  
    (c) Advances.—The Secretary of Transportation may borrow from the Treasury such sums as may be necessary, but not to exceed $30,000,000 on a temporary and reimbursable basis to implement subsection (a). The Secretary of Transportation shall reimburse the Treasury, without interest, as funds are deposited into the Digital Television Transition and Public Safety Fund under section 309(j)(8)(E) of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 309(j)(8)(E)) and made available to the Secretary under subsection (a).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that making funds "available" between Secretaries, or borrowing from the Treasury, is a form of coordination. Every actor here (Secretary of Commerce, Secretary of Transportation, the Treasury) is inside the federal government, and the section only governs funding transfers and advances for the essential air service program. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: to the Secretary of Transportation for use in carrying out the essential air service program for that fiscal year.

qwen_block.w: This section describes the transfer of funds between two federal agencies (the Department of Commerce and the Department of Transportation) based on appropriation levels. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, or the public. The interaction is strictly intra-governmental.
qwen_block.s: If the amount appropriated to carry out the essential air service program under subchapter II of chapter 417 of title 49, United States Code, equals or exceeds $110,000,000 for fiscal year 2007 or 2008, then the Secretary of Commerce shall make $15,000,000 available... to the Secretary of Transportation

opus.w: This section only moves money: it sets a funding trigger, transfers funds from Commerce to Transportation, and lets the Secretary of Transportation borrow from and repay the Treasury. Every actor involved is a federal official or agency, so the interaction never crosses the federal boundary. There is no consultation with outside parties, no public comment or hearing, no rulemaking, and no right to sue, so the funding mechanics do not count as participation.
opus.s: The Secretary of Transportation may borrow from the Treasury such sums as may be necessary, but not to exceed $30,000,000 on a temporary and reimbursable basis to implement subsection (a).
opus.b: **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section describes money moving between the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Transportation and the Treasury, including borrowing and repaying. That could look like coordination before a decision. But every party involved is inside the federal government. No state, community, airline or member of the public is consulted, and the section contains no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes a mandatory transfer of funds between two federal cabinet secretaries (Commerce and Transportation) based on a specific appropriation threshold. It involves only federal officials and agencies. There is no requirement to consult with, coordinate with, or obtain input from any party outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). Intra-agency coordination is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: If the amount appropriated to carry out the essential air service program under subchapter II of chapter 417 of title 49, United States Code, equals or exceeds $110,000,000 for fiscal year 2007 or 2008, then the Secretary of Commerce shall make $15,000,000 available... to the Secretary of Transportation
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the transfer of funds between the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of Transportation constitutes "coordination" or "consultation" between federal agencies. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. Furthermore, there is no mention of any outside party (states, public, experts, etc.) being involved in the decision to transfer these funds.
